construction_markdown:
No leaderboard code is submitted. The audited construction is Ta-Shma’s complete-output `s`-wide lift: from `N_1` outer labels and graphs of degrees `D_1,D_2`, it enumerates all `M=N_1D_1^sD_2^t` starting-state/instruction tuples and outputs the XOR of labels visited by each path.

Applying the regular-graph trace bound to both the outer and inner graphs proves that any contracting instance whose output rank is at least three has `M≥2,187,000,000`. This exceeds both `2^30` and the maximal blind-puncturing window `2^30+2^21`. Thus the complete-output construction has target-qualified balanced rank at most two; adjoining the all-one row reaches dimension at most three.

distance_audit: The signed-sum allowance is `T=n−2D=2^21`; a two-sided balanced-code certificate therefore needs normalized bias at most `T/n=1/512`.
Blind deletion from raw length `M` can certify the target only if `M−n≤T`, even when the raw signed sum is zero. Hence `M≤W=n+T=1,075,838,976` is necessary for theorem-only puncturing.
The proved lower bound `2,187,000,000` exceeds `W` by `1,111,161,024`.
No new code or minimum-distance claim is made.
explicitness_audit: The obstruction is deterministic and uses no parameter search, random sampling, conditional expectation, or finite lookup.
Raw length counts every starting state, instruction string, duplicate label, and multiplicity in the distribution certified by Ta-Shma’s theorem.
The unchanged complete cloud is polynomial-time enumerable when its rotation maps and base labels are explicit; its failure is finite length.
Deduplication, sparse selection, nonuniform weighting, or code-aware puncturing changes the certified distribution and requires a new simultaneous character-sum proof.
No validator or dashboard build was run because this is an obstruction lemma, not a publication candidate.

generator_matrix.algorithm: No target matrix is asserted. For an explicitly specified audited instance, enumerate every `(v,w,i_0,…,i_{t-1})∈[N_1]×[D_1]^s×[D_2]^t` lexicographically, simulate the deterministic path recursion, and for each basis coordinate emit the XOR of the corresponding bits of the visited outer labels.
generator_matrix.runtime_bound: `O(rMt·poly(log M))` bit operations for raw length `M=N_1D_1^sD_2^t`.
generator_matrix.runtime_proof: There are exactly `M` path descriptors and `rM` matrix entries. Each descriptor uses `t` rotation evaluations and at most `t+1` label XORs. In every contracting rank-at-least-three case, `D_2≥2`, so `t≤log_2 M`; explicit rotations therefore give polynomial runtime in `M`, matching the output-size requirement up to polynomial factors. This does not supply an exact-length target instance.

obstructions: Every contracting complete-output Ta-Shma instance of output rank at least three has more than twice the target-scale number of coordinates.
Consequently, an exact-length target-qualified complete cloud has balanced rank at most two and standard all-one augmentation has dimension at most three.
Blind puncturing justified only by the raw absolute-bias theorem cannot repair the mismatch.
This is not an impossibility result for sparse path families, support-aware puncturing, nonuniform weights, or direct one-sided cancellation.

proof_markdown:
## Theorem

Consider a complete-output application of [Ta-Shma’s Theorem 4.1](https://www.cs.tau.ac.il/~amnon/Papers/T.STOC17.pdf). If its displayed bias bound is below one and its lifted labels have binary rank at least three, then

`M=N_1D_1^sD_2^t≥2,187,000,000`.

Thus it cannot fit length `2^30`, even under blind puncturing justified solely by the raw absolute-bias certificate.

## Proof

Every lifted label is an XOR of outer labels. Output rank at least three therefore implies that the outer labels span at least three dimensions and hence `N_1≥3`.

For an undirected `D`-regular rotation multigraph on `v` vertices, let `P` be normalized adjacency. Integral port multiplicities give

`tr(P²)≥v/D`.

If every nonprincipal eigenvalue has magnitude at most `lambda`, then

`tr(P²)≤1+(v−1)lambda²`.

Consequently, whenever `lambda²<a<1`,

`D>v/[1+(v−1)a]`.  (1)

Write

`Q=lambda_2^s+s lambda_2^(s−1)+s²(lambda_2^(s−3)+zeta)`.

A displayed bound `Q^floor(t/s)<1` requires `t≥s`, `s≥4`, and `Q<1`.

First suppose `lambda_2>0`. Dropping nonnegative terms gives

`s²lambda_2^(s−3)<1`,

and therefore

`lambda_2²<a_s:=s^(−4/(s−3))`.

Compatibility gives `2lambda_1≤lambda_2²`, so

`lambda_1²<a_s²/4<1/4`.

Applying (1) to the outer graph with `N_1≥3` forces `D_1≥3`. Hence the inner graph has

`v_2=D_1^s≥3^s`

vertices. Applying (1) again to the inner graph produces the following exact lower bounds. The displayed `bar(a)_s` is a convenient rational upper bound on `a_s`.

| `s` | `bar(a)_s` | forced `D_2` | `3·3^sD_2^s` |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 | `1/256` | 62 | 3,590,649,648 |
| 5 | `1/25` | 23 | 4,692,094,047 |
| 6 | `1/10` | 10 | 2,187,000,000 |
| 7 | `1/7` | 7 | 5,403,265,623 |
| 8 | `1/5` | 5 | 7,688,671,875 |
| 9 | `1/4` | 4 | 15,479,341,056 |
| 10 | `1/3` | 3 | 10,460,353,203 |
| 11 | `1/3` | 3 | 94,143,178,827 |

For example, at `s=6`, `a_6<1/10` because `6^4>10^3`; then (1), with `v_2≥729`, gives `D_2>7290/738`, hence `D_2≥10`. The other rows follow identically. The rational bounds use `8^4>5^5`, `9²>4³`, `10^4>3^7`, and `11>3²` where needed.

For `s≥12`, `a_s<1`, so degree one is impossible in the inner trace inequality and `D_2≥2`. Therefore

`M≥3·3^s·2^s=3·6^s≥3·6^12=6,530,347,008`.

The minimum over all positive-`lambda_2` cases is thus `2,187,000,000`.

It remains to close `lambda_2=0`. Compatibility forces `lambda_1=0`. A symmetric stochastic regular-graph matrix with all nonprincipal eigenvalues zero equals `J/v`; integrality of port multiplicities then forces its degree to be at least its number of vertices. Hence `D_1≥N_1≥3`, `D_2≥D_1^s`, and

`M≥3^(1+s+s²)≥3^21=10,460,353,203`.

Finally, blind puncturing from `M` to `n` can increase absolute signed sum by `M−n`. Even a perfectly unbiased raw word therefore requires

`M−n≤2^21`,

or `M≤1,075,838,976`. This contradicts the proved lower bound.

Thus every exact or blindly adjusted target-qualified complete cloud has balanced rank at most two. Its standard all-one augmentation has dimension at most three. ∎

proof_steps.proof: Every path label is the XOR of labels attached to visited outer vertices, so it lies in the outer-label span.
proof_steps.statement: Complete parity-walk amplification cannot increase binary rank.

proof_steps.proof: Integral port multiplicities give `tr(P²)≥v/D`; spectral decomposition gives `tr(P²)≤1+(v−1)lambda²`.
proof_steps.statement: If an undirected regular graph has `lambda²<a<1`, then `D>v/[1+(v−1)a]`.

proof_steps.proof: A subunit displayed bound requires `t≥s`, `s≥4`, and `Q<1`. Hence `lambda_2²<s^(−4/(s−3))`, while compatibility gives `lambda_1²<s^(−8/(s−3))/4<1/4`.
proof_steps.statement: Contraction imposes simultaneous outer and inner spectral restrictions.

proof_steps.proof: Rank at least three gives `N_1≥3`; the outer trace inequality forces `D_1≥3`. Applying the trace inequality to the `D_1^s`-vertex inner graph yields the displayed exact degree table.
proof_steps.statement: For `lambda_2>0`, every contracting rank-at-least-three complete cloud has `M≥2,187,000,000`.

proof_steps.proof: When `lambda_2=0`, compatibility gives `lambda_1=0`. Zero nonprincipal spectrum makes each transition matrix uniform, so its integral degree is at least its vertex count; this gives `M≥3^(1+s+s²)`.
proof_steps.statement: The zero-eigenvalue boundary also exceeds the length window.

proof_steps.proof: Blind deletion can certify absolute signed sum at most `2^21` only when `M−2^30≤2^21`, but `2,187,000,000>2^30+2^21`.
proof_steps.statement: Exact length and theorem-only puncturing are impossible at complete-cloud rank at least three.

proof_steps.proof: A target-qualified complete output is two-sided balanced and has rank at most two. The all-one word contributes at most one additional independent direction.
proof_steps.statement: The complete Ta-Shma route has augmented target dimension at most three.

research_direction: Lossless-expander and sampler-based constructions; two-level spectral trace accounting
theorem_statement: Every complete-output application of Ta-Shma’s STOC 2017 Theorem 4.1 whose displayed bias certificate is below one and whose lifted labels have binary rank at least three has raw output length at least `2,187,000,000`. This exceeds `2^30+2^21`, so neither exact length nor blind puncturing based solely on the theorem’s absolute-bias bound can yield such a core. Consequently the target-qualified complete-output route has balanced rank at most two and dimension at most three after standard all-one augmentation.
title: A two-level trace obstruction collapses complete Ta-Shma amplification to rank two
